Subject: Model fit + quantization trade study - post-call recap

Thanks again for your time today, Tom - great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Key takeaways:
- Workload: ~1k daily active users for the assistant, typical prompt length ~120 tokens, and peak concurrent sessions expected 30-50.
- Quality bar: high - product team prioritizes response correctness and factuality over minor latency wins.
- Throughput target: ~60 qps sustained during peak; latency SLO target 200-300ms p95 for generation.

Recommended starters for model/eval: 
- Llama 2 13B (instruction-tuned) - baseline for cost/latency.
- Mistral Instruct 7B - promising for cost-sensitive inference.
- Falcon 40B or equivalent higher-capacity model as a quality upper bound if you want strict accuracy thresholds.

Quantization / throughput options to evaluate (we discussed tradeoffs):
- AWQ (4-bit) - best throughput with careful calibration; some risk of narrow quality regressions on longer, factual prompts.
- GPTQ (4-bit) - generally conservative, fewer surprises but slightly slower than AWQ in our runtime.
- FP8 paths - potential middle ground on newer hardware (FP8 gives speed with less aggressive precision reduction).

Attachments: I attached the prompt set we discussed (finwave_prompt_set_v1.csv) and a short sample MOP (redwood_mop_recommendation.pdf) with the initial eval plan.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) You share a small representative test corpus (or confirm we can use the prompt_set_v1 as-is).
2) We run a 2-week trade study: baseline (no quant), GPTQ-4, AWQ-4, and FP8 runs across the prompt set with automated metrics + small-scale human evals on ~100 prompts.
3) Align on objective metrics (exact match / factuality score / p95 latency) and pass/fail thresholds.
4) Quick sync to review results and agree on rollout (canary vs immediate).

Can you confirm permission to run these evals on the prompt set and any constraints (IP, redaction needed)? Also, any calendar windows next week for a 30-min technical review?

Thanks -

Tom / Marissa - quick technical follow-up from the infra side after reviewing the prompt set and running an initial micro-benchmark: 

Summary of early results (attached: quant_results_awq_vs_gptq.xlsx):
- Baseline (FP32) Llama 2 13B: p95 gen latency ~240ms on our 1xA100-80GB reference node, throughput ~55 qps with beam/greedy config matching your production settings.
- GPTQ-4 conversion: quality delta across seed prompts negligible (<1% on our automated F1/factuality proxy), p95 latency improved ~18% (to ~200ms), throughput ~68 qps.
- AWQ-4 conversion: throughput improved further (~85 qps) and p95 latency down to ~165ms, but we observed a small set of prompts (~4% of the test set) where the generation was noticeably shorter or missed a factual clause. These look recoverable with prompt-engineering or selective higher-precision fallbacks.
- FP8 experiment on newer HW: latency ~170ms p95, quality similar to GPTQ-4 for most prompts but more stable on longer context windows.

Interpretation / recommendation:
- For FinWave's stated quality-first bar, I'd recommend running the full trade study but gating any AWQ-based rollout behind a targeted human-eval pass and an automatic fallback to a higher-precision variant when a confidence metric is low.
- If cost is the prime driver and you can accept a small controlled regression, AWQ-4 gives the best unit economics. GPTQ-4 is a safer middle ground. FP8 is promising on next-gen infra if you plan to run in that environment.

Estimated cost for 2-week trade study (compute + 500 human-eval samples): approx $8k- $12k - we can tighten this estimate after scoping exact run counts.

Next steps from my side:
- Run full-run conversions and automated evals across the provided corpus (needs final redacted file from FinWave).
- Produce a short report with per-prompt diffs, latency/throughput curves, and recommended canary strategy.

If that plan looks good I can start as soon as you confirm the redacted dataset.

Thanks -
Rishi
